figures.caption: Figure 6.4. Discharge voltage profiles comparing all eight samples at a). C/20, b). C/5, c). C/2, and d). 1C. MIX composites are shown as solid lines; MF core-shell composites as dashed lines. Colors follow the Ragone plot convention: LMO (olive), LFP (dark red), MIX samples (blue shades), MF samples (warm shades). Both architectures show the expected dual-plateau behavior at C/20—LMO near 4.0 V and LFP near 3.4 V—with plateau lengths scaling with LFP content. As the rate increases, MIX samples retain well-defined plateaus and near-theoretical capacities, while MF samples show progressive plateau collapse proportional to LFP loading, particularly severe at 30 wt% LFP above C/5.

MIX composites (solid lines) follow an additive trend closely tracking LMO, with capacity offset proportional to LFP content. MF composites (dashed lines) match MIX performance at C/20 but diverge sharply above C/10—MF 30%LFP drops to ~43 mAh/g at 0.5C while MIX 30%LFP retains ~95 mAh/g. 4b). Discharge specific capacity as a function of LFP wt% and discharge rate. The grey translucent surface shows the theoretical mixing-rule prediction based on measured pure LFP and LMO capacities. MIX samples (square markers, blue shades) sits at or slightly below the theoretical surface at all rates; MF samples (spade markers, orange shades) fall progressively below it at rates ≥ C/10, with MF 30%LFP delivering less than 1% of its theoretical capacity at 2.5C.

figures.caption: Figure 6.6. Long-term galvanostatic cycling at 0.5C for all sample variants. Pure LMO (olive) and MIX composites (solid blue shades) exhibit stable, gradual capacity fade consistent with baseline Mn dissolution rates, with higher LFP fractions providing marginally improved retention. MF core-shell composites (dashed warm shades) universally show accelerated fade—MF 05%LFP deteriorates from ~85 mAh/g to below 40 mAh/g within 100 cycles, a faster decline than bare LMO despite the presence of the LFP coating. Higher MF loadings fail even earlier due to insufficient accessible capacity at 0.5C. This demonstrates that the continuous core-shell interface actively destabilizes the electrode rather than providing the intended protection. [card note: the plotted MF 05%LFP curve and the text end at ≈68.5 mAh/g, not below 40]

figures.caption: Figure 6.7. Discharge voltage profiles during 0.5C cycling for all MIX and MF variants, color-coded by cycle number (light = early, dark = late). MIX composites (blue shades) maintain well-preserved profile shapes throughout, exhibiting only uniform horizontal contraction as cycles progress, consistent with capacity loss without kinetic degradation. MF composites (red shades) display progressive profile shape evolution, with discharge curves becoming increasingly narrowed and steeply sloped over cycles, indicating the growth of polarization and cumulative Li⁺ transport restriction caused by the mechanofused LFP shell.
